what: the observed-like (obslike) mass spectrum: GWTC-3 POWER LAW+PEAK medians and their mapping onto darksirens-core powerlaw+peak; generator name --mass_spectrum gwtc3_pp

paper.citation: Abbott et al. (LVK), Phys. Rev. X 13, 011048 (2023), arXiv:2111.03634
paper.model: POWER LAW+PEAK, App. B 1 b, Eqs. (B4)-(B7); priors Table VI

m_min.where: Sec. VI E (fit without GW190814 and GW190917)

m_99.where: Sec. VI A (derived 99th percentile of m1)

sigma_m.note: no median in any version's text or tables (the paper says only that the Gaussian's mean and width agree with GWTC-2); 3.6 is the brief's value, said to be the data release's median; not verified here

m_max.note: no median quoted (the paper reports m_99 instead); 87 is the brief's value; not verified here. With alpha 3.5 the power law above 77 Msun holds 3e-4 of it

paper.earlier_arxiv_versions: v1/v2 (Nov 2021) quote alpha = 3.4 +0.58 -0.49, mu_m = 34 +2.3 -3.8, beta_q = 1.1 +1.8 -1.3, m_99 = 45 +11 -6.2, and (without the two low-mass events) m_min = 2.5 +0.67 -0.44, delta_m = 7.8 +1.9 -4.0; v3/v4 and the journal version quote the values used here

mapping.dm_min: delta_m (core's low-mass taper of the power law AND the pairing taper of m2 = q m1 for both components, as GWTC-3's Eqs. B4 and B7)
mapping.dm_max: core's high-mass taper width of the power law; GWTC-3 cuts P sharply at m_max, so it is set to core's prior floor 0.01 Msun (DM_MAX bounds [0.01, 20])
mapping.structural_differences: core leaves the Gaussian untapered and truncates it to [1, 200] (GWTC-3: tapered by S); <S>_G = 1 - 1e-9, so immaterial

core_theta_order: v1 alpha m_min m_max dm_min dm_max mu_G sigma_G beta mu_chi sigma_chi gamma (v1 = POWER-LAW weight)
